RFC8950-3-2.note: The next hop is the VPN-IPv6 address with an 8-octet RD set to zero. TestParseMPReachNLRI_VPNWithIPv6NextHop decodes a zero-RD 24-byte next hop, and a decoder that skips the RD would pass whatever the RD holds. TestMPReachNLRI_RoundTrip_VPN encodes an IPv4 next hop (the RFC 4364 12-byte form, a neighbouring rule) and asserts only NH_Len = 12, never that the 8 RD bytes are zero. A writer emitting a non-zero RD passes both units. The 48-byte link-local form is untested.

RFC8950-4-1.note: Sentence: MUST only advertise IPv4 or VPN-IPv4 NLRI with an IPv6 next hop after ascertaining peer support for the relevant AFI/SAFI pair. Now proven on next-hop-self resolution: TestRFC8950IPv6NextHopFollowsTheNegotiatedPair drives Peer.resolveNextHop with ExtNH for 1/1 only, 1/128 only and neither, asserting the IPv6 address only for the licensed pair and ErrNextHopIncompatible with no address otherwise, so the VPN-IPv4 and per-pair clauses are covered. Still unproven: (a) an explicit next hop -- resolveNextHop returns NextHopExplicit unchecked ('validated by the wire builder'), and UpdateBuilder emits MP_REACH with the given next hop for any non-unicast SAFI (message/update_build.go) with no ExtNH test, so an explicit IPv6 next hop for VPN-IPv4 without the pair negotiated has no unit that would go red; (b) a forwarded route whose IPv6 next hop is left unchanged toward a peer lacking the pair. No unit builds or inspects an UPDATE.

RFC8950-4-2.note: MUST determine peer support through Capability Advertisement for the pair(s) of interest. TestNegotiateExtendedNextHop and ...Mismatch (capability/negotiated_test.go) prove both-advertise and remote-absent. An implementation that treated any remote ExtNH capability as support for every pair passes both tagged units. The untagged TestNegotiateExtendedNextHopMultipleFamilies tests per-tuple negotiation and would close the clause if tagged.

RFC8950-5-1.note: MUST NOT change the encoding of a next hop passed along unchanged. The non-compliant behaviour is the RR re-encoding the 16-byte IPv6 next hop. TestReactorForwardRRPreservesExtendedNextHop (reactor/forward_rr_test.go) asserts require.Equal(mpReach, attrs[14]) and the next-hop bytes 4:20, so any re-encoding goes red. Single-polarity positive per the row's marker.
